summary: Cannot run the closed loop: both subagent dispatch tools (Task and Agent) are disabled for this session ('disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here'), and the programmatic fallback (yarn loop) is unavailable because orchestrator/node_modules/@cursor is not installed and CURSOR_API_KEY is unset. No stage was dispatched, so no stage ran. Per team.md a stage counts as run only when dispatched via Task/Agent with subagent_type equal to the agent name AND the agent wrote its own handoff; doing the work in the orchestrator turn does not count. Loop paused at stage 1 (software-engineer) with zero completed stages. A read-only verification pass found one critical error in the incoming brief: the web Challenge components are NOT dead code (see findings).
goal: 1v1 Challenge screen: (1) replace the `displayName ?? username ?? "Someone"` placeholder with the shared climberDisplay(id, displayName) helper; (2) extend GET /api/users/search to accept an exact email OR an exact username.

feedback.message: Dispatch is impossible in this session: Task and Agent tools are both disabled, and the yarn loop path needs @cursor/sdk (absent) plus CURSOR_API_KEY (unset). The orchestrator cannot substitute itself for the 6 required team members.
feedback.action: Re-run /closed-loop in a session where the Task/Agent tool is enabled, or install @cursor/sdk and set CURSOR_API_KEY and run `yarn loop`, or explicitly instruct a single agent to do the work directly (accepting that review/security/QA gates will not run).

feedback.message: The incoming brief states that app/src/components/Challenge/{UserSearch,FriendRequests,FriendsList,PendingChallenges}.tsx are orphaned/dead code based on a grep for 'components/Challenge/...' returning zero matches. That is a false negative. app/src/components/Duel/DuelHome.tsx:36-39 imports all four via RELATIVE paths ('../Challenge/UserSearch'), and app/app/duel/page.tsx:3,16 renders DuelHome. All four web components are LIVE and reachable at the /duel route.
feedback.action: Treat the four web Challenge components as in-scope. Apply the climberDisplay swap to app/src/components/Challenge/FriendRequests.tsx:188,246 and PendingChallenges.tsx:186,240, and apply the email-or-username search change to app/src/components/Challenge/UserSearch.tsx as well as the mobile UserSearchSection.tsx. Shipping only the mobile half would leave /duel searching by email only.

learnings.insight: A reachability grep that only matches path-alias or absolute import forms ('components/Challenge/X', '@/components/...') misses relative imports. app/src/components/Challenge/* looked like dead code for exactly this reason; app/src/components/Duel/DuelHome.tsx imports it as '../Challenge/UserSearch' and app/app/duel/page.tsx renders DuelHome.
learnings.action: Never conclude a module is dead from one import-path spelling. Grep the bare basename (e.g. `rg -n 'UserSearch'`), then walk the importer chain up to an app/ route file before declaring anything orphaned.

learnings.insight: The 1v1 challenge UI is duplicated: app/mobile/src/components/challenge/* and app/src/components/Challenge/* both render friend requests, pending challenges, and user search, and both are live (mobile screen + /duel web route). The `?? "Someone"` placeholder exists in 4 mobile sites, 4 web sites, and 3 server-side notification sites.
learnings.action: Any change to challenge/friend UI behaviour must be applied to both trees in the same commit, and QA must exercise both the mobile screen and the /duel web route. Grep '"Someone"' across app/ to enumerate all 11 sites rather than trusting a per-file list.

learnings.insight: Dispatch capability was not checked until after loop/state.json was initialized, so state.json briefly advertised a running loop that could never run.
learnings.action: At loop startup, probe the dispatch tool with one cheap no-op call BEFORE writing loop/state.json; if dispatch is unavailable, write status 'blocked' immediately and never claim 'running'.
